correctness.rationale: I enumerated the cube vertices as binary triples and generated the twelve position swaps by counting differing coordinates. A separate packed-integer frontier enumeration, `cd /workspace && python3 q3_reproduction.py`, covered every permutation of eight labels. Besides constructing the layers it checked all legal neighbors differ in the resulting labels by one, and every nonidentity state has a descending neighbor: the first property gives a lower bound along any legal path and the second supplies a realizing path. Its outputs were the exact 13 shells (1,12,90,476,1903,5472,10388,11756,7347,2408,430,36,1), sole level-12 state (7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0), and transportation-gap counts (19064,18088,3144,24). This checks the entire finite state set independently of the supplied BFS code. A relabeling commutes with each position swap and sends the identity to any placement, so eccentricities, shell counts and the single-antipode conclusion transfer; each of the 40320 placements contributes to exactly one unordered diametral pair. The total travel is even because the numbers of tokens crossing the two parity parts in opposite directions agree, and one swap reduces travel by at most two. The claim is sequential, not a statement about matching layers. The supplied script uses int.bit_count (Python 3.10+), so its stated 3.9 minimum is a minor replay-documentation error; the independent replay does not rely on bit_count.

evidence: The constructive recursive bound (E.14) is not a sharp sequential Q3 census. Alon–Chung–Graham obtain rt(Q_n)≤2n−1, so the resulting general estimate of at most five matchings of size at most four only gives a sequential upper bound of 20 here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The complement permutation already needs 12 sequential swaps by the transport lower bound. The general upper bounds above do not certify 12 as an upper bound, let alone characterize equality or the deficit distribution.

value.rationale: Q3 is a canonical small interconnection graph; this is its full shortest-sequential-swap census, not a slice or sampled average. For evaluating routing heuristics it gives an exact worst-case cost, the geometry of its unique worst opponent, and exact failure frequencies of the ubiquitous transportation relaxation. The sharper information is not furnished by generic graph connectivity or parallel routing bounds; no higher-dimensional consequence is claimed.
